candidates.name: golang.org/x/perf/benchfmt Reader and UnitMetadataMap
candidates.proposed_use: Parse benchmark unit declarations incrementally into a unit-keyed metadata map and expose direction/assumption accessors to a benchmark consumer.

citations.section: Overview L201–206; Reader.Result/Scan/Units L385–405; UnitMetadata and UnitMetadataMap L500–549

candidates.opened_evidence: The API exposes metadata records and a normalized-unit map, with better={higher,lower} and assume={nothing,exact}. The parser reads key=value pairs and reports an error for differing values of the same unit/key.
candidates.remaining_adapter: Connect producer/CLI input and reporting. Supporting the frozen higher/lower=better/worse aliases and detecting contradictions across those differently named keys would require normalization not established here.
candidates.limitations: The documented direction spelling is an alternative canonical form, but the parser does not itself normalize arbitrary synonymous keys. No CLI -unit path or whole-contract completion was verified. Parser errors are nonfatal records that consumers must inspect; execution was not performed.

candidates.name: golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat
candidates.proposed_use: Consume benchmark unit assumptions when summarizing and comparing measurements.
candidates.opened_evidence: The command documents nonparametric statistics under the default assume=nothing and single-sample comparisons under assume=exact, warning on variation.
candidates.remaining_adapter: Supply unit metadata and integrate any required CLI declaration and direction-alias validation.
candidates.limitations: Benchstat is already explicitly named by the initial proposal, not a newly identified family. This section alone establishes neither all four direction formulations nor contradictory-alias rejection or CLI configuration.
